newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Tone mixed but bullish trade seen.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Tone mixed but bullish trade seen.

text.p: Some investors were taking big upside bets on the U.S. stock market through options on Monday, but the overall tone was not definitively bullish or bearish, options traders said.
At the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, one firm was buying a sizable amount of July 890, 895 and 900 calls of S&P 500 index futures-options, a floor trader said.
"These guys are stepping up and buying at the all-time highs. I would say it's pretty much a speculative bet," he said. "It could be some fund hedging but we haven't heard."
Investors' willingness to pay the high cost for those calls was a bullish sign, he said.
By about midday, the July 890 calls were trading at 29.30, the July 895 calls at 26 and the July 900 calls at 23.30.
But other than that big trade, dealers said investors were playing both sides of the market, with some taking on bullish positions but others buying puts for downside protection.
"It's speculation, but there are no big positions either way," one index options dealer said.
One institution was active in SPX puts recently but it had little influence on the broader market or investor sentiment, he said.
Some options analysts are raising warning flags as the market rolls on with barely a pause.
Lawrence McMillan, who publishes the Daily Volume Alert, said in a report Monday his momentum indicator had climbed above 500 for the first time ever.
"Most certainly, we are due for a sharp correction, but based on past history it may be only a brief one," he said.
McMillan, who also publishes The Options Strategist, explained that severely overbought markets tend to have short, sharp corrections, then trade sideways before moving higher.

Bu the market's action around the 900 level on the SPX, where open interest in the calls remains high, could be key to the near-term direction, said Moby Waller, an analyst at Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute.

"A blow significantly through this level without so much as a pause would be a clear signal that the rally will continue, while a stutter is likely to precede a consolidation period," he said in a report.
In afternoon trading, the SPX was up 0.69 at 893.96, off its 895.17 intraday high, which was a record.
September S&P 500 futures were up 0.75 at 904.20 after reaching 905.80, less than a point below their record peak.
Among other indices, the S&P 100 .OEX gained 0.25 to 872.03 after reaching a record 872.39 intraday high.
The Dow industrial average was down about four points at 7,778. The bellwether market measure has spent the day bouncing slightly above and below unchanged.
